title: Metabolic signatures of ferritin and TDP-43 co-pathology provide a mechanistic basis for stratified therapeutic approaches in ALS
funding_sources: Target ALS Early-Stage Clinician Scientist awardFS-2023-ESC-S2
data_availability_text: Data sharingAll data are available in the manuscript, tables and supplementary data.
sections_present: ultrahigh performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectroscopy (uplc-ms/ms):
stratification by ferritin and tdp-43 pathological burden defines distinct cohort subgroups.
pls-da model classifies absence or presence of tdp-43 and ferritin pathology with strong model performance.
concurrent tdp-43 and ferritin pathology produce a distinct profile of disrupted lipid, membrane, and energy metabolism.
single positive states engage divergent compensatory metabolic pathways, which are lost when ferritin and tdp-43 co-occur.
dual ferritin and tdp-43 pathology defines a distinct metabolically decompensated state.
single pathology states reveal distinct mechanistic pathways.
ferritin accumulation provides a metabolic–imaging bridge for precision medicine in als.
